TCS Q1 Results Disappoint Investors: Revenue Falls, Margins Rise
TCS shares dropped 5% after its Q1 FY26 results missed expectations. While revenue fell 1.6% QoQ, net profit rose 5.9% due to operational efficiency and cost control. Key reasons for the revenue dip include the end of the BSNL contract, global IT slowdown, AI transition, and rising attrition. Despite challenges, TCS is pushing forward with AI investments, large client deals, and long-term workforce planning.
